name: Troy
founder: Ilus, son of Dardanian king Tros and naiad Callirrhoe
primary_gov: As tribal monarchies, then as a bureaucratic monarchy, then as tribal monarchies.
secondary_gov: Lacked formal advisory councils, but likely relied on aristocratic elders for guidance.
religion: Apollo, the god light, prophecy, and healing.

name: Hungary
founder: Árpád, son of Magyar prince Álmos and an unknown mother
primary_gov: As a tribal monarchy, then as a feudal monarchy, then as a feudal oligarchy, then as a feudal monarchy.
secondary_gov: The Royal Council (“királyi tanács”), then by the Royal Chancellery (“királyi kancellária”), the Council of Lords (“főrendek tanácsa”), and the National Assembly (“országgyülés”). The Council of Lords later became the House of Magnates (“főrendiház”).
religion: Paganism, then converted to Roman Catholicism.

name: Sparta
founder: Lacedaemon, son of sky god Zeus and pleiad Taygete
primary_gov: As tribal monarchies, then as a diarchy. As the diarchy, each king descended from the Agiads or the Eurypontids.
secondary_gov: The Assembly (“Apella”), the Council of Elders (“Gerousia”), and the Overseers (“Ephorate”). The Assembly elected Elders for life and Overseers annually.
economy: Exported olive oil, wine, pottery, grain, iron, copper, bronze, wool, and leather. Imported tin and timber.
religion: Zeus, the god of thunder, law, and the sky.

name: France
founder: Clovis, son of Salian Frankish king Childeric and Thuringian queen Basina
primary_gov: As a feudal monarchy, then as an absolute monarchy, then as a mixed republic.
religion: Roman Catholicism, then converted to Protestantism.

name: Athens
founder: Cecrops, a half-serpent born from the ground
primary_gov: As tribal monarchies, then as an aristocratic oligarchy, then as a direct democracy.
secondary_gov: The Assembly (“ekklesia”) and the Council of 500 (“boule”). The Assembly was open to male citizens, while the Council had 500 elected representatives from 10 local tribes.
economy: Exported olive oil, wine, pottery, silver, lead, and bronze. Imported grain, timber, copper, tin, iron, wool, leather, fish, and slaves.
religion: Athena, the goddess of wisdom, strategy, and war.

name: Wales
founder: Rhodri, son of Gwyneddwyr king Merfyn and Powyswyr princess Nest
primary_gov: As tribal monarchies, then as a semi-feudal monarchy, then as a feudal principality under England.
secondary_gov: The Royal Court (“ilys”), then by the Prince’s Council (“cyngor y tywysog”). English conquest led to the Council of Wales (“cyngor cymru a’r gororau”).
religion: Paganism, then converted to Roman Catholicism.

name: Ithaca
founder: Arcesius, son of Phocian king Cephalus and Athenian princess Procris
primary_gov: As tribal semi-monarchies, then as a semi-aristocratic monarchy.
secondary_gov: Lacked formal advisory councils, but likely relied on aristocratic elders for guidance.
religion: Athena, the goddess of wisdom, war, and strategy.

name: Denmark
founder: Harald Bluetooth, son of Danish king Gorm and Danish princess Thyra

name: Thrace
founder: Thrax, son of war god Ares and an unknown mother
primary_gov: As tribal semi-monarchies, then as a tribal monarchy, then as an imperial province under Rome.
secondary_gov: Lacked formal advisory councils, but likely relied on aristocratic elders for governance.
religion: Bendis, the goddess of the moon and hunting; like Artemis.

name: Holy Roman Empire
founder: Charlemagne, son of Austrasian Frankish king Pepin the Short and Austrasian Frankish noblewoman Bertrada

name: Mycenae
founder: Perseus, son of sky god Zeus and Argive princess Danaë
primary_gov: As tribal monarchies, then as an aristocratic monarchy, then as a bureaucratic monarchy.
secondary_gov: Lacked formal advisory councils, but likely relied on government administrators and aristocratic elders for guidance.
religion: Poseidon, the god of earthquakes, oceans, and horses.

name: England
founder: Aethelstan, son of Anglo-Saxon king Edward the Elder and Anglo-Saxon noblewoman Ecgwynn
